correctness.rationale: For h>=3, \(H_i\)=N-s_i-1 >=1 for all parts. Within-part jumps change neither utility nor potential. For cross-part jumps, exact quadratic differences give Delta Phi=(\(R_t\)-\(x_it\))/\(H_i\)-(\(R_t\)-\(x_jt\)-1)/\(H_j\)=Delta utility. A mixed full part has red-plus-blue old utility 1 and red-plus-blue separate hypothetical target utility 1+1/\(H_j\), so at least one improves. Under monochromatic full parts, exact direct utility comparison gives the two non-strict inequalities, yielding a necessary and sufficient criterion. Disjoint counting yields the polynomial. For \(K_{2,2,b}\), the integer inequality reduces to 2 ceil(2(b-2)/3)<=b-1, true only b=2,3,5 for b>=2. A separate graph-based rational checker examined 35,349 configurations and 243,582 moves over 16 parameter instances; all checks passed. Universal validity follows analytically, not from finite checks.

value.rationale: This is a complete infinite-family characterization of a natural fractional heterophily jump game, not a parameter renaming: it proves exact potentiality for arbitrarily many types on nonregular complete multipartite graphs, determines precisely every two-color equilibrium including arbitrary unequal part sizes, provides all red-count coefficients, and exposes a concrete integer reentrance \(K_{2,2,3}\)/\(K_{2,2,4}\)/\(K_{2,2,5}\). The structural mechanism combines forced monochromatic full communities with vacancy-size-dependent incentive thresholds. No downstream theorem or broad uniqueness claim is needed.
